items.q: How does Big Sean reframe depression and low moods?
items.a: As **growing pains** — a blessing and **alignment confirmation**, not proof you're broken. Low mood signals you're out of alignment and meant for more.

items.q: Does "armor" mean critics stop affecting you?
items.a: No — things still hit you. The skill is building **armor** so you can drop baggage and **get back to work**, not numbness.

items.q: What is the "power of separation" for artists?
items.a: Separate **love of the craft** from how others receive it — Oscar or bomb shouldn't define the next move. Denzel Washington models outcome-independent next-step discipline.

items.q: What actually counts as the win?
items.a: **Creation and actualization** — having an idea and making it real is the win; impact and reception are a bonus. Fixating on critics distracts from the path.

items.q: What football-coach rule does Jay Shetty share for wins and losses?
items.a: **Cry one night** after a loss, **celebrate one night** after a win, then get back to training — don't live off past success or grief for weeks.

items.q: Where did Kobe Bryant find peace after basketball?
items.a: From a **new purpose**, not more trophies — peace comes from **purpose, not prizes**.

items.q: Is accepting your starting point the same as giving up?
items.a: No — **accept ≠ surrender**. Accepting where you are means you're ready to go somewhere else; **resistance to reality** creates the tension that blocks the next move.

items.q: What's the difference between chasing and attracting?
items.a: **Chasing** encodes the energy of the thing running away; **attracting** magnetizes via aligned action — even tiny completed intentions ("I need to shower") count.

items.q: Why does living for critics fail as a strategy?
items.a: Trying to please everyone is a **business you'll never succeed at** — you lose yourself to people-pleasing and still don't win approval. Hardest acceptance for Sean: what he can't control — how people perceive his art.
